newsitem.title: CHILE: Escondida workers end strike - spokesman.
newsitem.headline: Escondida workers end strike - spokesman.

text.p: Workers at Chile's Escondida mine have voted to end their strike and return to work as of Friday, a spokesman for the 350-member union said.
"We have voted to desist from the strike and return to work," said spokesman Pedro Rivero.

He declined to say if Minera Escondida Limitada, which has denied the two-week strike had any effect on production, made a new pay offer to the workers. Union chief Hugo Fernandez will give the reasons for lifting the strike later, said Rivero.
"Workers are returning to the job as of today (Friday), in accordance with each person's shift," said Rivero.

Under Chilean law, if more than 50 percent of the workers return to work voluntarily after two weeks on strike, the walkout automatically loses its legal status and an employer is free to fire the strikers. But before any firings, unions usually agree to lift the strike.
Rivero declined to say if that was what happened.
But Escondida officials said on Wednesday that the two-week provision would take on Saturday -- not Friday.
Officials at the mine, owned by Broken Hill Proprietary, have consistently denied the strike is having any effect on production, though they admitted it was slowing down operations.

The open pit mine, cathodes plant and copper port at Puerto Coloso near Antofagasta together employ about 2,000 people. Only about 15 percent of those were actually on strike, but the stoppage was still closely watched by industry specialists as a sign of organized labor's strength at the new, non-unionized and mainly foreign-owned mines across northern Chile.
